svg.title: University Tech Transfer Odds Narrow Fast
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-tech-transfer-odds-funnel; chapter number: 6; chart type: funnel; title: University Tech Transfer Odds Narrow Fast; subtitle: From office economics to the rare million-dollar invention; caption: Nelsen calls tech transfer a lottery where only a dozen US offices make money at any time; Salk's director says two or three inventions drive 80-90% of revenue.; assumptions note: Each stage is a separately reported percentage with its own population (offices, research dollars, or disclosed inventions). Stages are ordered by size to show narrowing odds, not as one cohort passing through.; note: Attributed to Columbia TechVentures (Herschwitz), the MIT Technology Licensing Office (Millar-Nicholson) and OSU Center for Clinical and Translational Science.; stages: label: Offices losing money gross; value: 84; display: 84% of US university offices; conversion: Starting odds for a typical office; detail: Herschwitz's figure, contrasted with Columbia sitting in the top 2-3 earners for 20 years.; label: Offices covering operating costs; value: 14; display: 14% of US offices; conversion: Few offices break even on operations; detail: Offices like the MIT TLO rarely cover their costs.; label: Licensing return per research $1; value: 4; display: 4 cents per $1 of research funding; conversion: $58B revenue across AUTM surveys, 1991 to 2022; detail: Millar-Nicholson's math on 30 years of AUTM survey results against university research funding.; label: Stanford disclosures reaching $1M; value: 0.8; display: 0.8% of disclosed inventions; conversion: Best-in-class benchmark; detail: Success defined as at least $1M in cumulative revenue.; label: Ohio State disclosures reaching $1M; value: 0.1; display: 0.1% of all inventions ever disclosed; conversion: The home-run tail; detail: Provisionals go in before publication at $1,200-$1,500; non-provisionals cost $15-30K.

text.title: University Tech Transfer Odds Narrow Fast
text.tspan: University Tech Transfer Odds Narrow Fast

rect.title: label: Offices losing money gross; value: 84; display: 84% of US university offices; conversion: Starting odds for a typical office; detail: Herschwitz's figure, contrasted with Columbia sitting in the top 2-3 earners for 20 years.
label: Offices covering operating costs; value: 14; display: 14% of US offices; conversion: Few offices break even on operations; detail: Offices like the MIT TLO rarely cover their costs.

label: Licensing return per research $1; value: 4; display: 4 cents per $1 of research funding; conversion: $58B revenue across AUTM surveys, 1991 to 2022; detail: Millar-Nicholson's math on 30 years of AUTM survey results against university research funding.
label: Stanford disclosures reaching $1M; value: 0.8; display: 0.8% of disclosed inventions; conversion: Best-in-class benchmark; detail: Success defined as at least $1M in cumulative revenue.

label: Ohio State disclosures reaching $1M; value: 0.1; display: 0.1% of all inventions ever disclosed; conversion: The home-run tail; detail: Provisionals go in before publication at $1,200-$1,500; non-provisionals cost $15-30K.

text.title: Assumptions: Each stage is a separately reported percentage with its own population (offices, research dollars, or disclosed inventions). Stages are ordered by size to show narrowing odds, not as one cohort passing through.
